AlternateTargets: the phrase that cuts off every stream
Senses.Note: The expression names both an action and the named middle member of a three-phrase test: its job is to stop every current rather than cover everything or follow the waves.

Occurrences.Kwic: 既能截斷眾流，可以超今冠古。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X64/X64n1260.xml). Outline Record of the Successive Patriarchs. Exact utterer: Yuanwu Keqin. In an address requested by a prince, Yuanwu Keqin says that one who can cut off every stream can surpass present and past.

Occurrences.Kwic: 德山緣密圓明禪師上堂：我有三句語示汝諸人：一句函蓋乾坤，一句截斷眾流，一句隨波逐浪。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X85/X85n1593.xml). Orthodox Line of the Chan School. Exact utterer: Deshan Yuanming. Deshan Yuanming presents cutting off every stream as one of three phrases shown to the assembly.

Senses.Explanation: Cutting off every stream is the middle of a recurring three-phrase set and also a direct claim about speech that permits no continuation or turning back. Guizong Huitong, Shangfang Qiyue, Ruiyan Zhicai, and Rifang Shangzuo answer direct questions about the stream-cutting phrase with an iron mountain, a weeping woman, “Good,” and a crosswise staff. Deshan Yuanming explicitly places it between covering heaven and earth and following the waves. Yuanwu Keqin uses it as the action of a solitary proclamation and as a capacity that surpasses present and past.
